label: Text A
title: Youth Unemployment and Skills Development in a Rural Community
provenance: Constructed CAPS-aligned classroom stimulus for educator review
content: In the Eastern Cape village of Qumbu, 68% of youth aged 18–24 are unemployed, according to a 2023 community survey conducted by the local youth forum. Many school leavers lack access to further education or training due to financial constraints and limited information about available opportunities. Thandi, a 19-year-old who passed matric in 2022, has been searching for work for eight months without success. She holds a National Senior Certificate but has no work experience or specialised skills. The village has one FET college 45 kilometres away, but transport costs are prohibitive. Recently, a non-governmental organisation launched a free six-month digital literacy and entrepreneurship programme targeting out-of-school youth. Participants receive training in basic computer skills, CV writing, and small business planning, along with a stipend for data costs. Thandi has applied but is unsure if she will be selected due to high demand. Local leaders note that while such programmes help, long-term solutions require government investment in rural infrastructure and youth-friendly economic zones.
context: This scenario reflects real challenges faced by rural youth in South Africa regarding transition from school to work or further study. It aligns with CAPS Grade 12 Life Orientation topics on citizenship education, human rights, responsibility, and the world of work, particularly focusing on unemployment, skills development, and access to opportunities.

2023 community survey by local youth forum
Thandi, 19, passed matric in 2022, unemployed for 8 months
No work experience or specialised skills despite NSC
Nearest FET college 45 km away, transport costs prohibitive
Free six-month NGO digital literacy and entrepreneurship programme
Training includes computer skills, CV writing, business planning, data stipend
High demand for programme, selection uncertain
Local leaders cite need for government investment in rural infrastructure and youth economic zones

label: Visual Text B
title: Decision-Making Framework for Post-School Pathways
provenance: Constructed CAPS-aligned classroom stimulus for educator review
content: [DIAGRAM DESCRIPTION: A flowchart titled 'Choosing My Path After Matric' with three main branches from a central decision point: 'Further Education', 'Learnership/Internship', and 'Entrepreneurship/Job Seeking'. Each branch leads to sub-questions: Under 'Further Education': 'Do I meet admission requirements?', 'Can I access funding (NSFAS, bursaries)?', 'Is the institution accessible?'. Under 'Learnership/Internship': 'Is it in my field of interest?', 'Does it offer a stipend?', 'Is it accredited?'. Under 'Entrepreneurship/Job Seeking': 'Do I have a viable business idea?', 'Do I have start-up capital or support?', 'Do I have work-seeking skills (CV, interview)?'. Each path concludes with outcome boxes: 'Proceed with preparation', 'Seek guidance and upskill', or 'Re-evaluate goals'. Arrows show feedback loops to reassess based on answers.]
context: This visual tool supports learners in making informed decisions about post-school pathways, a key component of the Grade 12 Life Orientation curriculum under 'Development of the self in society' and 'Career and career choices'. It encourages self-assessment, consideration of practical barriers, and goal-setting based on available resources and personal circumstances.
usable_evidence: Flowchart title: 'Choosing My Path After Matric'
Three main pathways: Further Education, Learnership/Internship, Entrepreneurship/Job Seeking
Sub-questions under Further Education: admission requirements, funding access (NSFAS/bursaries), institution accessibility
Sub-questions under Learnership/Internship: field alignment, stipend availability, accreditation status
Sub-questions under Entrepreneurship/Job Seeking: viable business idea, start-up capital/support, work-seeking skills (CV, interview)
Outcome options: Proceed with preparation, Seek guidance and upskill, Re-evaluate goals
Feedback loops allowing reassessment based on responses
